tools.description:
Get a paper's PDF now, through every route including the browser and
paid tiers, and queue its conversion by policy; the one tool that acts.
Reading a paper not held already starts its free routes, so this is for
"now", for a copy the free routes missed, or for a url the caller found
(the PDF at that URL is kept for this paper after a check that it is the
paper). Returns the result if it finishes within eight seconds; otherwise
returns a durable queued/running response while the fetch continues.
Repeating the call joins that request. Then paper_status or read_paper.
tools.name: library-mcp_fetch_paper

tools.description:
Find papers: the one search for papers, anywhere — one ranked list over
the library, the ePrint archive and paper-search's indexes (OpenAlex,
Semantic Scholar, arXiv, Crossref, DBLP, Scholar), merged by identity,
every hit registered. Each result says what is held of it — not held,
original, text, card — and the verb that applies next.

Depth: `limit` papers from `offset` on, up to 500 a call; each index is
asked as deep (up to 200 a source), so 100 or more papers on a topic
take one call of ten to twenty seconds. brief=True puts each paper on
one line (title, year, authors, identifier, what is held, where found),
for long lists; paper_status gives one in full.

Order: papers on topic first — a held title carrying the query's rare
words; a catalogued paper the library's own paper search ranks high,
by the words and the meaning of its title and abstract, its card and
its text, so a held paper is found though its title says it otherwise
(each says what matched it, with its best card item or passage and the
page); or a hit whose title and abstract carry most of the query's
words or that several indexes found — then the rest. `sort`: relevance
(default), newest, cited (the indexes' citation counts), or
cited_per_year (citations per year since publication: the recent work
others build on before old classics); the other sorts list the papers
on topic only. For the current state of the art give year_from with
cited_per_year or newest. An outside index finds a paper only by its
words; related_papers follows citations from a landmark paper among
the papers the library holds.

held_only keeps to papers the library holds, and asks no outside index,
so it answers in a second or two; sources narrows to any of
eprint, openalex, semantic_scholar, arxiv, crossref, dblp,
google_scholar. author matches any author of a paper, not only the
first, and keeps every result to that person's papers. This finds
papers; to search inside held texts use search_library, to read one use
read_paper. Nothing is fetched by finding. A query's list is kept for six
hours, so offset pages through the same list (offset=0 asks again when a
source failed); a query word that no paper found has in its title,
abstract, authors or year is named, which says the query as a whole
matched nothing.

paper_kind and topic keep to the papers the library has tagged so: each
catalogued paper has one kind and up to four topics, from fixed lists,
set by a model from its title and abstract or by a person; a paper an
index brought in today is tagged the next night. paper_kind is one kind
or a list, any of which: survey, book, thesis, construction,
cryptanalysis, security_proof, algorithms_math, implementation,
standard, other. topic is one topic or a list, and a paper must carry
every topic listed; for either of two, call once for each. Topics, by
group — hard problems: lattices, elliptic_curves_pairings,
rsa_factoring_dlog, multivariate, codes, isogenies,
hash_based_signatures; symmetric: block_ciphers, hash_functions,
aead_macs_modes, stream_ciphers, boolean_functions_sboxes; foundations:
foundations_prf_owf; what a paper builds: signatures,
mpc_secret_sharing, zero_knowledge, fhe, blockchains_consensus,
encryption_kems, anonymity_credentials, threshold, advanced_encryption
(ABE, IBE, broadcast, functional), key_exchange, commitments_vrfs,
ot_pir_oram, voting, obfuscation, protocols (TLS, messaging, PAKE,
authentication), searchable_storage; attacks: side_channels_faults,
quantum_algorithms, differential_linear, algebraic_attacks,
lattice_reduction, isd; implementation: software_performance, hardware,
masking_leakage, formal_verification, trusted_hardware_pufs;
cross-cutting: post_quantum; mathematics: number_theory,
algebraic_geometry, commutative_algebra, combinatorics_designs,
coding_information_theory, groups_algebra, complexity_algorithms,
quantum_information, analysis_probability. paper_status shows a
paper's kind and topics.

A call answers within about 50 seconds. When an index is still answering
then, the reply lists what came in time, says so, and the search goes on:
call again with the same arguments (or with only search_id, the id the
reply names) a minute or two later, and the full list comes back at once.
tools.name: library-mcp_find_papers

tools.description:
What the papers around one — those it cites and those that cite it —
imported, grouped by the cited paper, the most importers first, with a
record each. The entry point when an investigation starts from a paper
rather than a description: the mathematics its neighbourhood has
already reached for. side as in search_library(kind="imports").
tools.name: library-mcp_imports_near

tools.description:
What one paper imported, from where, in its own words (direction
"out"), or what held papers took from it and how they put it (direction
"in"): every import record of the paper, grouped by the other paper. The
records are citing sentences with their neighbours, statements restated
with their source named, and card items naming a reference; each has
its page. Use it on a paper you are validating to see what it leans
on, and on a mathematics paper to see how cryptographers have used it.
limit is the number of other papers listed (30, up to 200).
tools.name: library-mcp_imports_of

tools.description:
The card of one processed paper, under its kind and topics: its problem, methods, results,
assumptions, limitations, how it positions itself against earlier work,
and the questions it leaves open — each a plain sentence with the quote
from the text that supports it and its page. For the numbered theorems
verbatim use paper_statements; for the page around an item use read_paper.
tools.name: library-mcp_paper_card

tools.description:
A temporary signed URL to a held paper's original (kind="pdf") or to
its whole text as Markdown (kind="text"): GET it directly, no header
needed; it expires in 30 minutes. For a paper not held, fetch_paper
first; to read page by page, read_paper.
tools.name: library-mcp_paper_file

tools.description:
The notes people made on a held paper's passages in the library's web reader, by page: who wrote
each, when, the passage it is on, and what it says. Read-only; a note is a reader's own comment, not the
paper's text. To read the page around a note, read_paper(identifier, start_page=N).
tools.name: library-mcp_paper_notes

tools.description:
How held papers position themselves against one: for each held paper
that cites it from a reference list the library has read, its card's
positions item toward it (improves, breaks, generalizes, corrects,
builds-on or compares, with the statement and the quote) or its method
item (what it took), and the citing sentence — one reply in place of
related_papers followed by a card per citer. The descendants of an
attack, the uses of a theorem, the responses to a scheme.
tools.name: library-mcp_paper_positions

tools.description:
The reference list of one held text: each entry resolved to a held
paper, with the sentences that cite it, or kept as written when nothing
matched. References resolve by DOI, ePrint ID, NIST URL or title; an
unresolved entry is never guessed. Entries known only from the OpenAlex
index are listed after the ones read from the text. For papers citing
this one use related_papers.
tools.name: library-mcp_paper_references

tools.description:
The numbered theorems, lemmas, propositions, corollaries, conjectures and
definitions of one held text, verbatim, each with its page.

kind narrows: "statements", "definitions", or one kind such as "theorem".
Statements are extracted by their labels, with no model, and read on
across a page break while their sentence is unfinished. "[end unclear]"
marks one that stops mid-sentence; "[math unreliable]" one whose
mathematics the conversion lost; "again, first on p. N" a label that
stood before (a restatement). For the surrounding page use read_paper.
tools.name: library-mcp_paper_statements

tools.description:
One paper: its authors (every one known), identifiers, abstract, its kind and topics (the lists
find_papers names), how far it has come — known,
original kept, text, processed — the fetch routes tried, and what applies
next. No side effects. identifier is any scheme: an ePrint ID (2024/1234),
a DOI, an arXiv ID, an OpenAlex ID (W…), nist:…, or a URL. To get its
text use fetch_paper; to read it use read_paper.
tools.name: library-mcp_paper_status

tools.description:
Read a held text as complete Markdown pages, not search results.

Pass the identifier and start_page=1 to begin; follow the returned next
start_page to continue. page_count is 1-5. Page numbers are physical PDF
positions from 1, not printed labels. The header names the tier the text
came from. A block whose mathematics the conversion lost (HTML entities,
dollar signs written out, math glyphs strung among letters) is followed by
a note to read it in the PDF (paper_file). A paper not held is queued for
its free fetch routes and the reply says to read again in a minute. To
find a phrase inside the text use search_in_paper; for its theorems and
definitions use paper_statements.
tools.name: library-mcp_read_paper

tools.description:
Papers that cite one ("cited_by") or that it cites ("cites"): from
the reference lists the library has read — with the citing sentence —
and from OpenAlex, every paper it knows (each registered, so paper_status
and read_paper take it); each line says which route, what is held and
how cited it is. The one tool for who cites a paper: paper-search's
paper_citations is its engine.

`sort`: library (default: the papers whose reference lists the library
read first, the most cited by held papers first, then OpenAlex's most
cited), newest, cited (OpenAlex's counts), or cited_per_year
(citations per year since publication, among the 200 most cited: the
recent work built on a landmark paper before old classics). For the
current state of the art after a paper, give year_from with
cited_per_year or newest. `limit` up to 500 from `offset` on, one kept
list paged; brief=True puts each paper on one line. held_only keeps to
the citations the library holds. To see what a paper imported from its
neighbours use imports_near; to find papers by words use find_papers.
A call answers within about 50 seconds; when the index's listing takes
longer, the reply says so and the listing goes on: call again with the
same arguments a minute or two later for all of it.
tools.name: library-mcp_related_papers

tools.description:
Find a literal word or phrase inside one held text, case-insensitively.

Hyphens, dashes and spaces count alike ("baby-step giant-step" finds
"baby-step-giant-step"), and a phrase may run across a line break.
LaTeX markup does not count: "δ-correct if", "delta-correct if" and
"$\delta$-correct if" all find "$\delta$-\emph{correct} if", and
"Lemma 7" finds "Lemma $7$".
Pass words that appear in the text, not a question. Results carry physical
page numbers. No match means the phrase was not found, not that the text
is unavailable. To read sequentially use read_paper; to search across all
held texts use search_library.
tools.name: library-mcp_search_in_paper

tools.description:
Search what the library extracted from every held text, by words and
by meaning: quoted hits with their paper, page and kind, ranked as units.

kind is "passages" (statements, definitions and paragraphs, with card
items beside them), "statements", "definitions", "cards" (the card items
alone), one statement kind such as "theorem", or "imports": papers found
through the words with which held papers cite them — put that query as
an importing paper would write it, the objects and the property in
words, and if nothing fits, as the other field names them. side keeps
"mathematics", "cryptography" or "any" — for imports mathematics by
default, for the other kinds any (a side keeps the papers classified to
it and those not classified yet). paper_kind and topic keep the hits of
papers tagged so, with the lists find_papers names (paper kinds:
survey, book, thesis, construction, cryptanalysis, security_proof,
algorithms_math, implementation, standard, other): a paper of any kind
listed that carries every topic listed; for imports, the cited papers.
Pass words, not a question. To find papers by title use find_papers; to
read the page around a hit use read_paper.
tools.name: library-mcp_search_library
